text:
maya: Heads-up: I'm putting together an RFC for on-prem package finalization semantics. core problem: what does it mean for a package to be "applied" in airgapped clusters?
chris: Good. We've hit ambiguity between 'image pulled' and 'activation acknowledged by control-plane'. customers expect a clear notion of completion.
zane: Suggest we split 'apply' into 2 phases: local-activate and control-finalize. local-activate = local voters agree; control-finalize = control-plane records global active state.
maya: That maps to real needs. But race conditions if control-plane is unreachable on finalization. We need deterministic behavior for operators.
ida: Can we introduce 'finalization_mode' in manifest: {strict_control, local_then_sync, manual_confirm}? default strict_control for compliance customers, local_then_sync for smaller infra.
rebecca: Support: manual_confirm helps compliance teams that want human signoff before global finalize. Also helps when staging in isolated racks.
chris: Implementation detail: define 'voter' list in manifest (explicit IDs). activation quorum uses count or percentage, eg "quorum: {mode: count, value: 2}" or {mode: percent, value: 70}. That avoids implicit K8s pod counting.
zane: Add 'activation_window_seconds' during which late voters can still be included. defaults: quorum: {mode: percent, value: 66}, activation_window_seconds: 600.
maya: please stop spacing my name :)
maya: :) also need receipts. local agents should emit a signed activation receipt with a nonce and ttl. control-plane will validate receipts before finalizing. sample: {
  "voter_id": "zone-a-node-3",
  "package": "pkg-2026-03-22-rc1",
  "ts": "2026-03-22T08:12:00Z",
  "nonce": "n-xyz",
  "sig": "..."
}
ida: receipts are good. Also need a retention window and an audit trail. For manual_confirm mode, UX should force an audit comment on the finalize action.
chris: Edge: what if a voter is permanently removed but still listed? propose tombstone flag per voter plus optional auto-tombstone policy after N deploy cycles. default tombstone_policy = manual.
rebecca: Ops: auto-tombstone must be opt-in per cluster via admin policy. Compliance customers will never enable it.
zane: Failure modes tests: partitioned cluster where two subgroups each think they have quorum under local_then_sync. when control-plane comes back, we must detect conflicting finalization and mark package as 'conflict' requiring operator resolution.
maya: agreed. add 'conflict' state and a reconciliation flow: list conflicting receipts, show timelines, and a one-click merge or abort. also record a metric conflicts_total.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: observed trend: ~4% of onprem upgrades hit transient partitions for <7m. recommendation: default activation_window_seconds=900 for resilience.
ida: security note: receipts must be signed with node keys and validated against node registry; rotation and revocation policies must be documented.
chris: rollout UX: console shows per-voter state, quorum progress bar, and a 'suspend finalization' action to pause automatic finalize until manual check.
rebecca: support runbook: if control-finalize fails, show guidance: 1) confirm control-plane connectivity 2) check late receipts 3) if safe, use 'force finalize' with audit note.
maya: tiny nit: wording 'force finalize' -> 'force_finalize' API should require reason param.
maya: next steps: I'll sketch manifest schema and state machine diagrams in RFC. reviewers: chris, zane, ida, rebecca. ops-bot: include your partition metrics.
ops-bot: noted. will attach sample telemetry.
zane: I'll draft test matrix for conflict scenarios and retention edge-cases.
chris: I'll review for API surface and failure semantics.
rebecca: I'll coordinate with support for runbook and customer communication templates.
ida: ping me when draft is up; I'll add KMS/key rotation text.
maya: thanks all. posting RFC draft later today. :thumbsup:
